label: sec:categorical-mass-foundations-intro
html:
The preceding section established Reidemeister invariance of mass on the Borromean test case. We now lay the categorical foundations for all subsequent mass calculations. Mass constitutes a categorical invariant. It equals the Markov trace of a distinguished element of the Hecke algebra, splits along the descent involution into a base-level term plus a transient blow-up correction, and admits a recursive symbolic reducer with a disjoint-product property for multi-atom composites.

This section decomposes mass under the descent involution, culminating in the structural identification of the categorical mass with \mathrm{tr}_M on H_n(q) (categorical mass = Markov). It fills out the algebraic backbone with the Gröbner–Shirshov normal form trace evaluation, Hecke branching decompositions, and the recursive symbolic Markov-trace reducer. Finally, it aligns the Markov-Z spectrum with the mass-endomorphism conjecture and packages the mass functor as a global section (\Phi_n) ready for calibration. The subsequent section, Calibration and Algebraic Mass Formula, anchors this functor to physical units via three calibration inputs.
